items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1798

SPONSOR: BORRELLO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the actions of the
Panama central school district notwithstanding the failure to timely
file final building cost reports with the education department

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Legalizes, validates, ratifies and confirms the actions of the Panama
central school district regardless of the failure of such district to
timely file final building cost reports.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Allows the Education Department to consider the final cost
report for Panama Central School as legalized, validated, ratified and
confirmed for approved building projects completed prior to December 31,
2012 recognizing that the failure to submit the report in a timely
manner was an inadvertent administrative or ministerial oversight.

Section 2. Provides that the Commissioner of the State Education Depart-
ment shall not recover from the Panama Central School District any
penalty arising from the late filing of a final cost report pursuant to
section 31 of part A of chapter 57 of the laws of 2012, provided that
any amounts already so recovered shall be deemed a payment for money due
for prior years pursuant to paragraph c of subdivision 5 of section 3604
of the education law and shall be paid to the Panama Central School
District pursuant to such provision.

Section 3. Establishes that the act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Panama Central School District was assessed a $4.9 million penalty
as a result of a late final cost report from a 2005 capital project.  In
2005, the Panama Central School District completed a small maintenance
project that was closed out. In 2009, Panama Central School District
verified that this project was complete as shown on the state website.
Panama then started a new project in 2008.

In 2012, Panama Central School reviewed the state's website to find that
they had an "open" project with a substantial completion certificate
filed on August 28, 2002 and December 12, 2005. This information was not
previously made available to Panama Central School when they were clos-
ing out. their 2005 building project. This meant that Panama Central
School neglected to file a Final Cost Report for a building project with
the Office of Facility Planning of the State Education Department (SED)
within the established time frame.

In the 2013-14 State Budget, a plan was negotiated that allowed for a
10-year repayment plan to help the school manage what remained a tremen-
dous penalty for a small rural school district. Also provided in the
2013-14 State Budget was a $500,000 Supplemental Valuation Impact Grant
through the Education Department/Aid to Localities budget bill, which
was provided for again in the 2014-15 State Budget, the 2015-16 State
Budget, the 2016-17 State Budget, the 2017-18 State Budget, and the
2018-19 State Budget. This bill would forgive the remaining amount, $1.9
million, of the assessed penalty.  Without full forgiveness of this
penalty, the students who attend Panama Central School and the
District's taxpayers will be left holding the bag for administrative
oversights made over a decade ago.

With our small, rural schools already facing the heavy burdens of limit-
ed state aid, tax revenues and loss of enrollment and tax base, Panama
Central School faces particularly significant cash flow problems that
threaten its very operations if not addressed.

Panama and Clymer Central School Districts previously laid plans to
merge but the community had voiced tremendous concern over inheriting
Panama's final cost report penalties, leading to the merger being voted
down in November 2017. As such, locally, many individuals continue to
view this overwhelming obstacle as a key factor in the merger vote's
failure.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S.7034/A.8926 Vetoed Memo 56
2019: S.6365/A.5442 Vetoed Memo 124
2018: S.7383/A.9730 Vetoed Memo 357
2017: S.6779/A.8302-A Vetoed Memo 170
2015,2016: S.7416/A.10045 Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

$1.9 million in remaining final cost report penalty

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

VETO MESSAGE - No. 42
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Assembly Bill Number 4877, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  in  relation  to  legalizing,  validating,  ratifying  and
      confirming certain transportation contracts of  the  Corning  city
      school district"
 
Assembly Bill Number 6289, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the actions of the
      Monticello  central school district notwithstanding the failure to
      timely file final building cost reports with the education depart-
      ment"
 
Assembly Bill Number 6356-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT relating to legalizing, validating, ratifying and confirming
      transportation  contracts  for  the  Baldwin  Union  Free   school
      district"

Assembly Bill Number 6360-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT relating to legalizing, validating, ratifying and confirming
      transportation  contracts for the West Hempstead Union Free school
      district"
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Senate Bill Number 396-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT relating to legalizing, validating, ratifying and confirming
      a transportation contract of the Oneonta city school district"
 
Senate Bill Number 1798, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the actions of the
      Panama central school  district  notwithstanding  the  failure  to
      timely  file  the  final  building cost reports with the education
      department"
 
Senate Bill Number 1867, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT relating to legalizing, validating, ratifying and confirming
      a transportation contract of the Fulton city school district"
 
Senate Bill Number 4963-A, entitled:

    "AN ACT relating to validating certain acts by the Pearl River union
      free school district  relating  to  final  building  cost  reports
      required to be filed with the state education department"
 
Senate Bill Number 6188-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT relating to legalizing, validating, ratifying and confirming
      a certain contract of the West Islip union free school district"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  These  nine  bills  would forgive certain violations of state law that
resulted in the repayment or withholding of expense-based  building  aid
and  transportation  aid  that  would  have otherwise been owed to these
school districts.
 
  Payment of expense-based aids to school  districts  is  calculated  as
part  of  the  state's  annual budget process. Because these bills would
alter the aids agreed to in the Enacted State  Budget  for  the  current
year, I am constrained to veto these bills.
 
  Previously,  action has been taken to address these types of aid with-
holdings in several  past  State  Budgets.  Legislation  in  2011  ended
prepayment  of  building  aid  without  final  cost reports, so that new
building aid clawbacks could no longer occur, and the Fiscal  Year  2013
Enacted  State  Budget  provided  amnesty for prior projects. The Fiscal
Year 2018 and Fiscal Year 2019 budgets also limited annual building  aid
withholding amounts and eliminated residual penalties for districts with
high  penalties as a percentage of operating budget. I welcome a conver-
sation with the Legislature as part of  the  upcoming  state  budget  to
address  these  aid withholdings once and for all, and to ensure the law
fairly reflects consequences to school districts.
 
  The bills are disapproved.                     (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
